title: Watch a key expire (TTL, lazy vs active expiry)
summary: Discover how Redis manages ephemeral data using millisecond TTL countdowns, active 10Hz sampling cycles, and passive lazy checks on read.

steps.title: Set a transient key with a 6-second expiration
steps.explanation: Attach a TTL using the EX flag. Under the hood, Redis stores the key pointer in an internal expires hash table alongside its millisecond UNIX timestamp deadline.

steps.title: Inspect the remaining Time To Live
steps.explanation: Execute TTL to observe the remaining lifetime in seconds. If the key exists and has an expiration, Redis returns a positive integer. (Returns -1 if persistent, -2 if gone).

steps.title: Observe lazy deletion after deadline expires
steps.explanation: Wait 6 seconds for the TTL to expire. When you query GET on an expired key, Redis tests the timestamp during lookup, deletes the key passively, and returns nil.
steps.hint: Wait for the 6-second timer to run out, then execute: GET play:session:temp
